div.l: Wel ryche he was astored / prevely
His lord he cowde wel plese / and sotelly
To yeve and lene hym / of his owne / good
And have a thank / and yeet a coot and a hood
In youthe he had lerned / a good mister
He was a wol wryhte / and a carpenter
This reve sat vpon a wol good stot
That was pomly grey / and hihte scot
A surcote long / of pers vp on he hadde
And bi his syde / he bare a rusty bladde
Of northfold norfold northfold was this reve / of which I telle
Biside a toıı̄un/ men clepyn baldyswelle
Tucked he was / as is a frere a boute
And evyr he rood / the hyndyrest of the route
A SompnourA Sompnour was ther / with vs in that place
That had a feer reed / cherubyn is face
For sausflem he was / with eyen narwe
As hoot he was and lecherous / as any sparwe
With scalled browes blak and pyled berd
Of his vysage / children were a ferd
Ther nas quyk syluer / lytarge ne bronston̄
Boras Ceruce ne oyle / of tartre noon̄
Ne onyment that wolde / clense or byte
That hym myhte helpyn ·/ of the whelkys white
Ne of the knobbis / syttyng on his his chekys
Wel loved he garlek oynoıı̄uns / and lekys
And for to drynke strong wyn / reed as blood
Than wolde he spek / and cry as he were wood
And whan that he wel dronken / hadde the wyn
Than wolde he spekyn / nor word but latyn
Afewe termes / hadde he to or thre
That he had lerned / out of som decre
